questions.q: Why does the OUTPUT clause exist for INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE?
options: Because those statements normally only report a row count, not the actual rows they affected
Because SELECT cannot be used after a write statement
Because WHERE clauses are not allowed without OUTPUT
Because it is required for every INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE to run
questions.explain: Unlike SELECT, write statements don't return rows by default -- OUTPUT lets them return the affected rows in the same statement.

questions.q: Which pseudo-table holds the OLD values of a changed row, available to DELETE and UPDATE?
options: deleted
inserted
archived
removed
questions.explain: deleted holds the row's values before the change -- available on DELETE and UPDATE, since both remove or replace an old value.

questions.q: Why can an UPDATE statement's OUTPUT clause reference both inserted and deleted, while INSERT and DELETE can each only reference one?
options: An UPDATE has both an old value and a new value for every changed row, while INSERT only has new values and DELETE only has old values
UPDATE is the only statement that supports OUTPUT at all
inserted and deleted mean the same thing and are interchangeable
OUTPUT on UPDATE requires a JOIN to a second table
questions.explain: INSERT only creates new values (inserted), DELETE only removes old values (deleted), but UPDATE replaces an old value with a new one, so both pseudo-tables apply.

questions.q: What does adding INTO to an OUTPUT clause do?
options: Sends the returned rows into a real table instead of just displaying them
Converts the write statement into a SELECT statement
Prevents the write statement from actually modifying any rows
Forces the statement to run inside a transaction
questions.explain: OUTPUT ... INTO <table> inserts the affected rows' values into a destination table, commonly used to build an audit or archive trail.

questions.q: In 'INSERT INTO dbo.LessonDemo (...) OUTPUT inserted.ProductID VALUES (...);', what does inserted.ProductID return?
options: The IDENTITY value SQL Server just generated for the new row, without needing a separate SCOPE_IDENTITY() call
The ProductID of the row that existed before the insert
NULL, because ProductID is never included in INSERT
The total count of rows in the table
questions.explain: OUTPUT inserted.ProductID returns the new row's generated identity value directly, in the same statement as the insert.
